shape/prompts/shaper.md.patch:
diff --git a/shape/prompts/shaper.md b/shape/prompts/shaper.md
index 3543b06..e0bdec9 100644
--- a/shape/prompts/shaper.md
+++ b/shape/prompts/shaper.md
@@ -33,7 +33,7 @@ Non-UI work and changes where reachability or visible behavior is irrelevant get
 - Work over a collection. When the request describes an operation over a collection of records of unknown size (for example an export, an import, a bulk update, a listing, a report or a sync), the acceptance package includes one scenario that runs the operation twice with different record counts (for example 10 and 100) and asserts that the work the operation does against its data store or external services (for example the number of queries counted through the framework's own instrumentation, or the calls counted by a counting stub) stays within the same stated upper bound for both counts, so that the work does not grow with the record count. The scenario uses the project's own test tooling, and the controls.json wrong implementation for it does that work once per record. Skip this scenario only with a `- none: <reason>` line in `## Tests` that says why the operation cannot grow with the record count. A request that does not process a collection gets no such scenario.
 - Invented literals. A route, helper, parameter, environment name, state name or number that neither the Request nor a tracked file states is not asserted by the acceptance: the step finds it at run time (for example by the visible text of a link or form) or asserts the observable behavior the Request names. A bound such as a query count or a size is added only when the Request asks for it. A sentence of intent.md never adds a mechanism (a single transaction, a count bound) the Request does not require. A refused `invented_contract` finding is rewritten into observable behavior on the next submission, not repeated: Kogen refuses it once, then drops a repeated literal from the checks and lists it on the approval card under "Literals chosen by the Shaper" as not stated by the Request.
 - Guarantees. When the Request states a guarantee (exactly once, never, always, at most once, at least once, every, no), a Decision states that guarantee in the Request's own words. Put any limit of the repository or of the receiver as a separate open limit beside the guarantee, never in place of it; a Decision that weakens the guarantee is refused.
-- Time target: 15 minutes is the usual guidance for shaping and 20 minutes is the upper end of the performance target, and each turn states the time elapsed and the target. The target is advice, not a stop: shaping continues past it whenever it can make progress, and a late package goes through the same checks. Plan the work to fit it: gather what you need in few turns, with independent reads and probes together, and submit early rather than late. Correct refusals promptly.
+- Time target: 15 minutes is the usual guidance for shaping and 20 minutes is the upper end of the performance target, and each turn states the time elapsed and the target. Crossing the target is never a stop, but converge inside it: plan the work to fit it, gather what you need in few turns, with independent reads and probes together, and submit a complete package in the first rounds, early rather than late. Once the elapsed time stated in the turn is within about 3 minutes of the usual target or past it, submit the best complete package you have and spend later rounds only on the refusals Kogen names, with no new exploration of files you have not read. A late package is still checked by every ordinary gate.
 - Request every independent read_file, search_text, list_files and probe call you need in one response, and do not re-read a file you have already read unless it changed.
 {{feasibility-guidance}}

files.shape/prompts/external-guidance.md:
# Time and parallel work

The shaping has a time target for all rounds together: {{budget}} minutes is the usual guidance and {{upper}} minutes is the upper end of the performance target. Each round's text states the elapsed time and the target. Crossing the target is never a stop, but converge inside it: submit a complete package in the first rounds, well inside the target. Once the elapsed time stated in the round is within about 3 minutes of the usual target of {{budget}} minutes or past it, submit the best complete package you have and spend later rounds only on the refusals Kogen names, with no new exploration of files you have not read. A late package is still checked by every ordinary gate.
Issue independent reads, searches and commands together rather than one at a time.
For broad reading across many files, you may run several read-only subagents in parallel on a fast model (for example Sonnet or Haiku) and ask each for the specific facts you need, with file and line references; write the package itself in the main session. Do not use subagents for small lookups the main session can do directly.
Read what the request and its acceptance need, not the whole repository; stop exploring once the package can be written.
